items.title: Bobby Watson interviewed by Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, January 19, 1996
items.q: You have Charles Atlas here and here, or you might be Charles Atlas here you know, where you don’t actually look physically strong but you know, where it counts, you’re like Charles Atlas you know?

ctx.x: there, get in there.” And so and then the guitar player said, “The whole idea is to jump in over your head, because that’s how you learn.” Tell us about that.

Well we always said you have to hang with that fast company and you’re right, you know, you get in with players that are better than you, they’ll make you play stuff you didn’t know you could play. And just because by contrast players that are not so good can bring your level down. And the thing I learned from doing a lot of clinics and playing with a lot of high school players, is my level definitely does drop. But it’s okay, because I’ve learned how to play on different levels and still be happy. And that’s a…

the top all the time? But it’s so nice when Harold, the drummer, or Victor Lewis, or all the guys I’ve had over the years, when they turn it out man, it just inspires you and takes you to another level you know.
